newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Columbia/HCA may have destroyed documents relating to the criminal investigation into its business practices.
* United Parcel Service and its Teamsters union agreed to return to the bargaining table.
* Wholesale prices fell 0.1 percent in July, while retail sales rose 0.6 percent.
* Bond prices rose, although stocks were mixed on Wednesday.
* Chrysler said the average price of its 1998 vehicle lineup will be 0.6 percent lower than its comparably equipped automobiles and light trucks.
* The new tax law may spark a comback for the old-style pension plan, benefits consultants said.
* Cali Realty agreed to buy 55 office buildings from New Jersey's Mack family for $900 million in cash and securities, plus assumed debt.
* Navistar reached a tentative pact with the UAW.
* Warner Music is expected to announce a wide-ranging employment pact with producer David Foster.
* Lucent said it will take a charge of $950 million related to its $1.8 billion acquisition of Octel Communications.
* SmithKline named David U'Pritchard research chief.
* Rubbermaid's Little Tikes unit sued Mattel's Fisher Price to block it from hiring two former executives.
* A Bank Indonesia official said the central bank abolished the 12 percent dollar-rupiah trading band.
* Sony plans a new format for storage disks for computer data.
* Vanguard said chairman John Bogle is formally turning over the company to his heir apparent, CEO John Brennan.
* Micron shares fell 15 percent Wednesday, after a Merrill Lynch analyst slashed his 1998 estimates for the company in half.
